articles.title: Consensus guidelines in the management of paediatric flexible flatfoot : a Delphi study of the British Society of Children's Orthopaedic Surgery.
articles.authors: Morrow EM, Bennet S, Morrison SC, Bridgens A, Mavrotas J, Brousil J, et al.
articles.population: British Society for Children's Orthopaedic Surgery members (consultant orthopaedic surgeons, registrars/fellows, allied health professionals and advanced nurse practitioners)
articles.sample_size: 169 clinicians in Round One, 167 in Round Two
articles.outcomes: 26 consensus statements on assessment and management of flexible flatfoot in children, covering assessment, conservative and surgical management
articles.take_home: Experts across the UK have agreed on guidelines for how to assess and treat flat feet in children, though there is still uncertainty about which specific surgical procedures work best. These guidelines provide a framework to help clinicians manage children's flat feet more consistently.

articles.title: Accuracy of Computer-Assisted Navigation in Total Ankle Arthroplasty Surgery Using Computed Tomography: A Short Report.
articles.authors: Rakauskas TR, Henderson AP, Meli G, Herbel C, El Masry S, Boux De Casson F, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing total ankle replacement surgery
articles.outcomes: Accuracy of computer-assisted navigation in positioning ankle replacement implants, measured by comparing planned versus actual postoperative implant positions using CT scanning
articles.take_home: Computer-assisted navigation achieved accurate positioning for most measurements, such as the angle of the implant and cut height, but had less precision for rotational alignment and some talar (ankle bone) positioning. The technique shows promise for improving consistency of implant placement in ankle replacement surgery.

articles.title: Operative Treatment of Quadrimalleolar and Quadrimalleolar-Equivalent Ankle Fractures: Radiographic and Clinical Outcomes Following Component-Based Operative Fixation.
articles.authors: Nam JH, Kim HS, Yeo ED, Lee SH, Jung KJ, Hong CH, et al.
articles.population: Patients with quadrimalleolar or quadrimalleolar-equivalent ankle fractures treated surgically
articles.sample_size: 36 patients (18 quadrimalleolar, 18 quadrimalleolar-equivalent) with minimum 12-month follow-up
articles.outcomes: Radiographic syndesmotic alignment on CT scan, Olerud-Molander Ankle Score (OMAS), visual analogue scale (VAS) pain scores, fracture union, and wound complications
articles.take_home: A systematic surgical approach to these complex ankle fractures resulted in good alignment and favourable outcomes, with patients reporting an average pain score of 1 out of 10 and ankle function scores of around 85 out of 100 at one year. All fractures healed successfully with only minor wound problems.

articles.title: Transmalleolar vs Portal-Based Minimally Invasive Tibiotalar Joint Preparation: A Cadaveric Study.
articles.authors: Patel AN, Durudogan E, Arave M, Harish M, Achay J, Huh J, et al.
articles.outcomes: Proportion of tibiotalar joint prepared (tibial plafond, talar dome, combined surfaces); distances to posterior tibial tendon, artery, and tibial nerve; neurovascular injury risk
articles.take_home: The transmalleolar technique prepared more of the top of the shin bone (94.7% versus 76.8%) compared with the traditional portal approach for ankle fusion surgery. Both techniques had similar safety profiles with no nerve or blood vessel injuries, suggesting the transmalleolar approach may offer improved joint preparation without additional risk.

articles.title: Implant Choice Impacts Initial Tibial Component Micromotion in Total Ankle Replacement: A Biomechanical Analysis.
articles.authors: Henry JK, Hoffman J, Villar R, Lu K, Kim S, Steineman BD, et al.
articles.population: Cadaveric matched pairs (6 men and 4 women, mean age 48 years)
articles.outcomes: Peak and mean micromotion at the bone-implant interface measured via digital image correlation and computed tomography imaging
articles.take_home: Stemmed tibial components in ankle replacements had significantly less movement at the bone-implant interface compared to low-profile components, with low-profile implants showing a rocking motion that may contribute to early mechanical failure.

articles.title: Efficacy and cost effectiveness of high volume injections with and without corticosteroid compared with sham for midportion Achilles tendinopathy (Inject trial): randomised controlled trial.
articles.authors: Malliaras P, Connell D, Boesen AP, Kearney RS, Menz HB, Morrissey D, et al.
articles.study_type: Single centre randomised controlled trial with economic evaluation
articles.population: Adults aged 18 years or older with midportion Achilles tendinopathy
articles.sample_size: 192 participants (64 sham, 63 high volume without steroid, 65 high volume with steroid)
articles.outcomes: Pain and disability using VISA-A score at 12 months; cost per quality-adjusted life-year; adverse events
articles.take_home: High volume injections with or without steroid did not improve pain or disability compared to sham injection at 12 months. Although steroid injections showed short-term benefit and potential cost savings, they were associated with worse outcomes at 26 weeks, so routine use is not recommended.

articles.title: Effect of a new functional insole compared to a common bedding insole therapy for plantar fasciitis: A prospective randomized multicenter study.
articles.authors: Hardt S, Brozat-Essen S, Vogt D, Krieger H, Kauffhold A, Wendlandt R, et al.
articles.outcomes: Pain and mobility measured using Foot and Ankle Disability Index, American Orthopedic Foot and Ankle Society score, and Visual Analogue Scale for pain at 0, 6, 12, and 24 weeks
articles.take_home: Both soft cushioning insoles and functional insoles were effective for treating plantar fasciitis, with 84.5% of patients showing significant improvement in pain and mobility. There was no difference in effectiveness between the two types of insole.

articles.title: Comprehensive digital debulking and reconstruction for pediatric foot macrodactyly.
articles.authors: Yu A, Huang L, Sardor O G'li RA, Ding W, Sun W
articles.population: Children with foot macrodactyly (abnormally enlarged toes)
articles.outcomes: Toe size reduction, AOFAS scores (57.9 to 77.3), Maryland scores (75.5 to 91.4), scar appearance, parental satisfaction, complications including skin necrosis, scarring, toe deviation and delayed healing
articles.take_home: A new single-stage surgical technique called Comprehensive Digital Debulking and Reconstruction successfully reduced enlarged toe size and improved function in children with macrodactyly, with most parents satisfied and low complication rates. This approach preserved the toes rather than requiring amputation.
